title: Powered by A.I., Google Changes Its Search Box for the First Time in 25 Years
partialText: Powered by a new Gemini A.I. model, the tech giant is overhauling its search box to answer longer queries, introducing a video-generation and video-editing tool and simplifying online shopping.

title: Son of Mango Fashion Chain’s Founder Is Arrested as Suspect in His Death
partialText: Isak Andic, the billionaire who built the Spanish brand, died while hiking with his son in 2024. News outlets had reported that the son was under investigation.

title: Inflation Fears Cloud G7 Economic Agenda as Iran War Persists
partialText: The United States and Europe were at odds over the Trump administration’s decision to ease oil sanctions on Russia.

title: Rising Energy Costs and Data Centers at Heart of NextEra’s Dominion Bid
partialText: NextEra’s proposed acquisition of Dominion Energy comes as Americans are paying a lot more for electricity, and data centers are demanding a lot more power from utilities.

title: Amazon E-Bikes Take Root in Manhattan and Brooklyn
partialText: Small companies that handle the final delivery are relying on them to skirt New York City traffic. Amazon plans to try the bikes elsewhere, too.

title: China Wants A.I. to Flourish, but Not at the Expense of Jobs
partialText: A series of precedent-setting rulings signals that Chinese courts are being enlisted to shield workers from displacement by artificial intelligence.

title: Tesla’s Semi Truck could Jolt the Trucking Industry
partialText: California truckers have expressed strong interest in the Tesla Semi because it costs much less and can travel further on a charge than electric trucks sold by established manufacturers.

title: ‘The Future of Truth’ Contains Quotes Made Up by A.I.
partialText: Steven Rosenbaum, author of “The Future of Truth,” said he had started his own investigation after The New York Times asked about the fake quotes.

title: Broadway’s ‘Giant,’ With John Lithgow as Roald Dahl, Turns a Profit in 10 Weeks
partialText: The fast success of this play, about the children’s author Roald Dahl, is a rarity on Broadway, where most shows lose money.

title: In Musk vs. OpenAI, the Real Winner was the Suit
partialText: It was the one thing on which every major player could agree.

title: Starbucks Korea CEO Fired Over ‘Tank Day’ Ad Evoking Country’s Brutal History
partialText: A marketing campaign called “Tank Day” coincided with the anniversary of a military dictatorship’s crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrators.

title: A FOMO Moment for Mythos
partialText: Those without access to Anthropic’s artificial intelligence model worry they’re more vulnerable to cyber attacks, a concern the company is seeking to address.

title: As OpenAI Celebrates Court Win Against Musk, Other Challenges Lie Ahead
partialText: A jury’s rejection of Elon Musk’s $150 billion lawsuit against OpenAI was a major hurdle crossed. But the maker of ChatGPT faces a list of other problems.

title: Bipartisan Bill Would Impose New Annual Fee on Electric Vehicles
partialText: A House transportation bill introduced this week would require owners of electric cars to pay $130 to cover the cost of road repairs.

title: Calls for ‘No Seed Oil’ Push Companies to Order Up Butter and Beef Tallow
partialText: Businesses are finding different (and more costly) ways to fry foods as shoppers demand alternatives to seed oils as part of the Make America Healthy Again movement.

title: On Blind, Anxious Tech Workers Get the Lowdown on Layoffs
partialText: On the website Blind, professionals share advice — and gallows humor — anonymously. It is chronicling the curdling of tech optimism.

title: Top Treasury Lawyer Resigns After Creation of ‘Anti-Weaponization Fund’
partialText: Brian Morrissey, the department’s general counsel, stepped down hours after the Trump administration announced the $1.8 billion fund.

title: Mamdani, the ‘Tax-the-Rich’ Mayor, Reaches Out to Titans of Finance
partialText: Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who has angered some corporate executives with his tax policies, has had a recent series of meetings with top business leaders.

title: TrumpRx Adds Generic Drugs, With Mark Cuban, GoodRx and Amazon
partialText: President Trump announced the addition of 600 medicines to his online drugstore as he appeals to Americans concerned about high drug prices and affordability.

title: New York Times Sues Pentagon for a Second Time
partialText: The Times is challenging a new requirement that reporters covering the military complex have an official escort, part of a broader legal challenge to the Pentagon’s press restrictions.

title: Federal Prosecutors Move to Drop Bribery Case Against Indian Magnate
partialText: Gautam Adani had been accused of lying to American investors about payoffs in India. The end of the case came as President Trump has signaled a transactional approach to justice.

title: Edmund Phelps, Who Upended the Way We View Inflation, Dies at 92
partialText: He won a Nobel in 2006 for challenging the conventional wisdom among economists that higher inflation was a necessary price to pay for low unemployment.

title: Shakira Is Found Not Guilty of Tax Fraud in Spain
partialText: A Spanish court ruled that the pop star was not a tax resident of Spain in 2011 and ordered the country’s tax authorities to return tens of millions of dollars to her.

title: Justice Dept. Sets Up $1.8 Billion Fund That Could Funnel Money to Trump Allies
partialText: The arrangement was denounced by critics as a slush fund for supporters of President Trump, possibly including Jan. 6 rioters.

title: Bobby Darin Musical Reaches a Rare Broadway Milestone: Profit
partialText: “Just in Time,” which for a year starred Jonathan Groff, is the first new musical from last season to make money for investors.

title: The Villain of This Year’s Commencement Speeches: A.I.
partialText: College students have interrupted graduation ceremonies to voice their fears about artificial intelligence. They’re not the only ones who are worried.

title: G7 Finance Ministers Look to Contain Iran Economic Fallout
partialText: Top policymakers were expected to discuss rising energy prices and sanctions policy at a critical summit in Paris this week.

title: My Boss Is an Alcoholic. What Should I Do?
partialText: Plus, a bona fide “kids say the darnedest things” moment at a company party.

title: Trump’s Approval Sinks Amid Unpopular War, Darkening G.O.P. Prospects
partialText: With the midterms nearing, President Trump’s approval rating has hit a second-term low as voters question his handling of the economy, according to the latest New York Times/Siena poll.

title: Insurers’ Delays in Approving Medical Care Persist, Despite Promises
partialText: Doctors and patients complain that the controversial practice of prior authorization for treatment and procedures is still widespread.

title: Oil Prices Climb and Bonds Falter as Iran War Raises Inflation Fears
partialText: Stocks and bonds wavered after President Trump issued a new warning to Iran.

title: Catastrophe Is Emerging in the World’s Most Vulnerable Places
partialText: The humanitarian relief system, decimated by cuts, faces a grave challenge as the Middle East war causes soaring costs for food, fuel and fertilizer.

title: NextEra Energy to Acquire Dominion, Creating a Utility Giant
partialText: The deal combining the companies in Florida and Virginia comes as demand for power is soaring, largely because of the rapid growth of A.I. data centers.

title: Peter G. Neumann, Who Warned of Computer Security Risks, Dies at 93
partialText: For decades, he criticized the industry’s lax attitudes toward computer security and individual digital privacy. He also developed solutions.

title: Straus Family Creamery Issues Voluntary Ice Cream Recall
partialText: Straus Family Creamery asked customers to throw out some tubs sold in May across 17 states. No injuries have been reported, the company said.

title: For Trump, Soaring Prices Test Voters’ Finances and Patience
partialText: Just months before another election that may hinge on the economy, the war in Iran has sent gas and other goods soaring.

title: The Iran War Is Crippling One of the World’s Wealthiest Nations
partialText: Iranian attacks and the stoppage of seaborne transit have paralyzed Qatar’s vital gas exports, stalling the economic pivots intended to anchor the country’s growth.

title: Senate Ruling Threatens Ballroom Funding in G.O.P. Budget Bill
partialText: Democrats announced Saturday night that the Senate’s top parliamentary referee had determined that the $1 billion provision did not comply with budget rules.

title: Shoppers’ Frenzy for ‘Royal Pop’ Pocket Watches Forces Swatch to Shut Stores
partialText: The pocket watches, a collaboration with the luxury timepiece maker Audemars Piguet, drew crowds to stores and malls around the world.

title: China Indicates Tariffs Were Discussed at Trump Summit
partialText: China’s Ministry of Commerce said Saturday that the countries had struck a preliminary agreement to reduce some tariffs, seemingly contradicting statements by President Trump

title: Thousands of FiveThirtyEight Articles Seemingly Vanish From the Internet
partialText: The influential polling analysis site was shut down last year, but an earlier archived version, fivethirtyeight.com, had lived on. Now the site is redirecting users to ABC News.

title: Oysters, Champagne and Billionaires Buying Art
partialText: When the European Fine Art Foundation alights in Manhattan, it’s something like a billionaire version of the classic television game show “Supermarket Sweep.”

title: U.S. Debt Is Now Bigger Than the Economy. That’s Not the Real Problem.
partialText: Washington quickly brushed off a startling milestone in a mounting problem.

title: Which Countries Are Profiting From the Iran War Oil Shock
partialText: An analysis of oil export data offers clues about which nations have benefited from higher prices, and which have lost a lot of revenue.

title: Josh Tyrangiel book excerpt: How OpenAI and Khan Academy Made a Chatbot
partialText: Inside a collaboration to bring artificial intelligence into the classroom.

title: Political Money Is Flowing to Influencers. But From Whom?
partialText: Social media stars have become a magnet for campaigns and political groups that want to push priorities without disclosing where their money is going.

title: NPR Podcast Host Ramtin Arablouei Exits Amid Workplace Inquiry
partialText: Ramtin Arablouei, a co-host of “Throughline,” left the network after an employee made a human resources complaint about his behavior.

title: Trump Administration Weighs $1.7 Billion Fund for Allies Investigated Under Biden
partialText: Critics denounced the highly unusual plan, which has yet to be finalized or approved, as a vast political slush fund financed by taxpayers.

title: Stock Market Rally Confronts Inflation and Higher Interest Rates
partialText: Despite accelerating inflation and possible interest rate increases, the S&P 500 has posted a long weekly winning streak, driven by strong corporate earnings. Can it last?
